name: Columbus, OH - Central US expansion
azure_region_intent: Capacity relief for Central US (East US 2 adjacency)
profile_text: Suburban Columbus parcel near an existing utility corridor and dense long-haul fiber. Strong state and local data-center tax incentives, ample municipal water for cooling, and low natural-hazard exposure apart from occasional severe thunderstorms. Grid interconnection queue is moderate; nearest metro is close, keeping latency low for Central US workloads.

name: San Antonio, TX - South Central US expansion
profile_text: Cheap ERCOT power with high wind and solar penetration and an unusually short interconnection queue, since ERCOT is a standalone grid with faster energization than the eastern interconnects. Streamlined Texas permitting and strong incentives. Main watch items are summer heat driving cooling load, medium flash-flood exposure, and constrained long-term water supply.

name: Quincy, WA - West US 2 adjacency
azure_region_intent: Low-cost hydro capacity near West US 2
profile_text: Rural central-Washington site with very cheap, nearly all-hydro power and a cool, dry climate ideal for free cooling. Downsides are distance from a major metro (higher latency, thinner fiber) and a long transmission interconnection queue tied to a needed substation upgrade. Cascadia seismic exposure is moderate. Novel location with few nearby comparable builds.

name: Phoenix, AZ - West US 3 expansion
profile_text: Established Phoenix-area data-center market with excellent fiber density, very low natural-hazard exposure, and strong incentives. Latency is low thanks to proximity to metro peering. The dominant risk is water: arid climate and tightening groundwater rules make water-based cooling contentious, pushing designs toward air or closed-loop cooling and lengthening environmental permitting.

name: Atlanta, GA - East US expansion
profile_text: Premier Southeast interconnection hub: the lowest latency and richest fiber of any candidate, close to a major metro. Trade-offs are higher power cost, a low-renewable grid mix, and complex multi-jurisdiction permitting that historically slows approvals. Medium exposure to remnant tropical storms and localized flooding.

name: Des Moines, IA - Central US expansion
profile_text: Iowa site with abundant low-cost wind power and generous incentives; a favored region for hyperscale builds. Cool climate aids cooling and water is plentiful. The two concerns are a long wind-driven interconnection queue (MISO study backlog) and high severe-weather exposure, including tornado and hail risk that raises hardening costs.
